system.name: ERM (Exemplar-Guided Reflection with Memory)
system.one_liner: Feedback-based prompt optimization with an exemplar-guided reflection prompt and two memories, feedback and exemplars, retrieved by priority score.

content.variant_note: three lettered panels filled with real prompts, outputs and scored memory entries from one maths word problem; operations shrink to Retrieval and Update arrow labels
content.argues: Keeping scored memories of feedback and of exemplars, instead of discarding them, lets prompt optimization reuse past information and pick better exemplars.
content.subject: An LLM turns failure cases into exemplars and feedback, which go into two scored memories that are retrieved to refine the prompt and to answer a new question.

lessons.what_to_learn: Show a text-driven method with its real text: colour each span of the prompt by role (instruction, feedback, exemplar, generated prompt) and keep the colours identical in every panel and in the memory the span is stored to, so the data flow can be followed by colour alone.
lessons.suits: Prompt-, memory- or reflection-based LLM methods where text artefacts flow between an LLM and stores.

evidence: As shown in Figure 1(a), we manually design an instructive meta-prompt.
We then propose Feedback Memory to store all feedbacks and assign a priority score to each of them
we store all exemplars in Exemplar Factory and assign a prior score to each piece.

summary: ERM (Exemplar-Guided Reflection with Memory) makes feedback-based automatic prompt optimization more efficient and accurate. Figure 1 shows its three parts as lettered panels filled with real text from one maths word problem. In (a) a meta-prompt makes the LLM write an exemplar (blue) and a feedback (orange); the feedback goes by an orange arrow to (b) Feedback Memory, the exemplar by a blue arrow to (c) Exemplar Factory. Each memory is a storage box of scored cards tied to an LLM prompt by Retrieval and Update arrows: (b) retrieves feedback to write a refined prompt, (c) retrieves exemplars to answer a new question. Spans are highlighted by role; robot and user icons mark the LLM and the prompt writer.
summary_zh: ERM 用带记忆的示例引导反思来优化提示词。图用三个带字母的面板和真实的数学应用题文本：（a）元提示让模型产出示例（蓝）与反馈（橙），分别经橙、蓝箭头存入（b）反馈记忆和（c）示例工厂，再用检索与更新箭头取用并更新带分数的条目。
notes: The caption in the context file is cut off after 'which guides'. The three panels map one-to-one onto the paper's three contributions (meta-prompt, Feedback Memory, Exemplar Factory), but arrows run from (a) to (b) and (c), so the figure is recorded as a pipeline with a worked example rather than as a contribution mosaic.
